question.text: A determinant is chosen at random from the set of all determinants of order 2 with elements 0 or 1 only. The probability that the determinant chosen is non-zero is

solution.text:
$\left|\begin{array}{ll}a & b \\ c & d\end{array}\right|=a d-b c=0$
Case $1: a d=b c=0 \rightarrow 3 \times 3=9$ cases
Case $2:$ ad $=\mathrm{bc}=1 \rightarrow 1$ case only
$\therefore$ Probability $=1-\frac{9+1}{2^4}=\frac{3}{8}$
